body: XSS: `url` is interpolated unescaped into an HTML attribute (`#{url}`), and the post is stored with cook_method raw_html, so it is rendered verbatim. A feed item/URL containing `'` (e.g. `http://x/'onmouseover='alert(1)`) injects attributes/markup. Escape with ERB::Util.html_escape / CGI.escapeHTML. Also `contents <<` mutates the caller's string in place (and raises on frozen strings); build a new string instead.

`cook` returns `raw` unchanged for raw_html posts, bypassing the whole cooking and sanitization pipeline. That HTML comes from external RSS feeds and remote pages (poll_feed calls CGI.unescapeHTML on it, and Readability keeps href/src, which allows `javascript:` URLs). It is then rendered with `raw` both in the forum and in embed/best, so it is a stored-XSS vector. Sanitize the HTML with a whitelist before storing or rendering it.

`i.content` is nil for plain RSS items that only have `<description>` (SimpleRSS only fills `content` for Atom/content:encoded), so `nil.scrub` raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole feed import. Fall back to `i.description`, and guard against nil.

`Kernel#open` with a string treats a value starting with `|` as a shell command, so this is command execution if the setting is ever `|cmd`. Use `open-uri`'s `URI.parse(url).open` (or Net::HTTP) instead of `Kernel#open`. The same applies to `open(url)` in TopicEmbed.import_remote. Also, `feed_key` is defined but never used, so there is no conditional GET / Last-Modified handling.

`open(url)` goes through Kernel#open (the pipe/command-execution risk), has no timeout or size limit, and does no scheme check: `import` only rejects non-http(s) URLs *after* the fetch. TopicRetriever only checks the host, so `ftp://embeddable_host/...` or `file://`-style URIs could be fetched. Validate the scheme first and use URI#open with timeouts.
The port check is wrong. `https://host:80/` or `http://host:443/` produces a URL with no port. Use `uri.port != uri.default_port`.

Protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn.example.com/a.png`) also start with '/', so they get rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/a.png`, which breaks them. Relative paths without a leading slash (`images/a.png`) are not handled at all. Use `URI.join(url, href)` instead of the prefix concatenation (the same applies to img src below).

On update, the result of `revise!` is ignored, but `content_sha1` is updated anyway. If the revision fails, later polls will never retry. The topic title is also never updated when the feed title changes.

There is a race: the controller enqueues a retrieve job on every uncached request, and PollFeed also imports. Two concurrent imports of the same URL both create a topic/post, then the second `create!` hits the unique index and raises. Depending on transaction nesting, that can leave an orphaned topic or fail the job. Handle RecordNotUnique or take a lock.

Every request for an unknown embed_url enqueues a job, and the loading page reloads every 30s, so each viewer generates a job every 30s. embed_url is arbitrary user input and is not validated against embeddable_host before enqueueing. Throttling only happens inside the job, so the job queue can be flooded. Validate the host and throttle before enqueueing. Also, the spec (embed_controller_spec.rb:43) expects TopicRetriever to be called synchronously, so it will fail against this implementation.

Access control relies on the Referer header. Many browsers/sites send no Referer (Referrer-Policy, HTTPS->HTTP), so legitimate embeds will be rejected. The header is also trivially spoofable outside browsers. Also, `X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL` is not a valid value; to allow framing, omit the header or use CSP `frame-ancestors` restricted to embeddable_host.

Interpolating `request.referer` into an inline JS string is fragile: HTML escaping is the wrong escaping for a JS context, and the full referer URL (path/query) is used as targetOrigin. Pass an origin built from SiteSetting.embeddable_host, with the value escaped via `j`/`escape_javascript`.

This origin check is a substring test. `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin)` passes for any origin that is a prefix of discourseUrl, e.g. `https://forum.example.co` when discourseUrl is `https://forum.example.com/`. Compare exact origins instead (parse discourseUrl and check `e.origin === expectedOrigin`).

`<%- end if %>` is a syntax slip. `end if` followed by a newline makes the *next* generated ERB statement the modifier-if condition. It only works by accident because the output append returns a truthy value. Use `<%- end %>`.
`setnx` followed by a separate `expire` is not atomic. If the process dies between the two calls, the key never expires and the URL is throttled forever. Use `$redis.set(key, '1', nx: true, ex: 60)`.

Every retrieve for an unknown URL synchronously re-runs the whole feed poll: it fetches and processes the entire feed, and that can happen repeatedly because staff bypass the throttle. This duplicates the hourly PollFeed job and is expensive. Consider only fetching the single URL, or rate-limiting the feed poll itself.

This edits an existing, already-shipped migration to add `force: true`. On any environment that re-runs it (e.g. a rebuild or a migration replay), that silently drops the existing top_topics table and its data, while sites that already migrated never get this change. Don't modify existing migrations. The new create_topic_embeds migration also shouldn't use `force: true`.
`embed_url` is a varchar(255) with a unique index, so longer URLs (common with query strings) will fail to insert and the import will raise. Use `text`, or validate the length.

This behavior change regresses the Disqus importer. The `--category` option was removed, `created_at` from the export is no longer applied, and every thread now triggers a live HTTP fetch of the article (failures raise and abort the import). Also, if the embed already exists, `import_remote` returns the existing post and all Disqus comments get re-imported as duplicates.
